title: Chapter 189: Rivalry
html:
Chen Ge removed his shirt, and the two nurses attached the audio recorder and heart monitor. After a brief test, several fluctuating traces appeared on the screen in the center of the hall. The proprietor pointed to them. “HR and PR indicate heart and pulse rates. SpO2 is peripheral oxygen saturation, an estimate of blood oxygen. RESP measures respiration, and TEMP is body temperature. Together, these readings let us observe changes in your emotional state clearly and objectively.”

After putting on his clothes, Chen Ge shrugged. “Can we start now?”

“The entrance is on the hall’s left, and the exit is on the right. We’ll meet you there,” the proprietor explained. “A guide inside will tell you what to do.”

“All right.” Chen Ge entered Tian Teng Medical School. Watching him go, the proprietor smiled. They had staged similar events in Xing Hai, where the monitor traces rose and plunged like a roller coaster. Combined with screams broadcast over the speakers, the readings allowed those outside to share the visitor’s fear.

“What an interesting fellow.” He quietly locked the door, then messaged the actors inside that their prey was approaching and ordered them not to hold back.

…

The room darkened as the door closed. Chen Ge waited for his eyes to adjust before moving forward. The first set depicted a security station. A uniformed guard sat with his back to Chen Ge, facing a blood-spattered monitor whose flickering images appeared to show the hospital interior.

This was an orientation room, designed to establish the attraction’s backstory and draw visitors into its narrative.

The key to moving forward should be the security guard. This setup is quite interesting.

Chen Ge approached the security booth, leaned toward its only window, and called inside, “Boss, what are you watching?”

At the sound of his voice, the guard slowly turned. Sweat covered his face. Pointing a trembling finger at the monitor, he stammered, “Th-there…”

A stutterer’s character setting? Very professional.

Chen Ge entered for a closer look. The monitor cycled through ominous headlines: Patients Mysteriously Leap from Hospital; Corrupt Doctors Sell Organs on Black Market; Confirmed Dead Return the Following Day. Considerable effort had gone into the presentation, which even included surveillance footage.

In the video, a white-clad woman staggered through a dark hospital corridor, head bowed and face hidden behind black hair. One moment she stood far away; the next, clever editing placed her close to the camera. At the three-second mark, her grotesque face filled the screen.

“There’s a ghost!” the security guard who sat behind Chen Ge screamed.

The guard’s timing was perfect, honed through countless repetitions. Chen Ge sighed and shook his head. “Excellent setup, but she might frighten me if she wore red.”

Female Red Specters held a special significance for Chen Ge. The video ended with a floor plan, showing that visitors had only to follow a prescribed route.

Such linear design was efficient but less engaging than the freedom to explore offered by Chen Ge’s attraction. After memorizing the map, he turned to leave. The sight of the guard made his eyes narrow and his heart rate rise slightly.

The guard now wore a thin ghost mask resembling the face from the monitor. He stared silently at Chen Ge, who stared back. “If you have nothing to say, move along. Don’t waste time.”

“Our Haunted House is really haunted. If you stumble across anything weird, remember to holler at the camera!” the security said seriously, and it did not sound like he was lying.

“Can you be more specific? What kind of ghost?” Chen Ge scanned the booth. A flashlight and several tools lay beneath the counter, apparently intended for visitors, though the guard showed no inclination to hand them over.

“You’ll understand soon enough. The path begins to your left. Push open the wall, and your investigation into Tian Teng Medical School’s secrets will officially begin,” the guard said mysteriously before ushering Chen Ge out.

“A real ghost? At most, it would be a lingering spirit.” Chen Ge muttered words the guard could not understand, pushed the wall open, and continued. The attraction was full of mechanisms; the wall closed behind him under remote control.

The details are on point; no wonder they’re so popular.

The orientation room alone had impressed Chen Ge, and he wondered whether he could adapt some of its ideas for his own Haunted House.

Beyond the wall lay a long, narrow corridor, roughly half normal width because of the limited space. Most striking was a desiccated “female corpse” hanging in the center, warning visitors of the danger ahead.

The hallway probably served as a buffer, allowing guests to brace themselves for the next scare—a considerate design. Chen Ge approached the body, then stopped.

In one corner, outside a visitor’s natural line of sight, stood an inconspicuous steel box. Most people would focus on the hanging corpse and overlook it entirely.

There has to be someone hiding inside the box. After being scared inside the security stop, they would be tense. When they first passed through the door, their attention would be dominated by the female body, and when they tried to walk past the body, a ghost would jump out at them from the box hidden in the corner. That’s quite interesting.

A ruthless design had met a man unfamiliar with the concept of restraint. The contest between cunning and shamelessness had officially begun.

I seem to have rediscovered the childhood joy of visiting a Haunted House.Chen Ge leaned his body against the wall. Since the actor was hiding inside the box, Chen Ge’s position was exactly inside his blind spot.

As he edged closer, Chen Ge ignored the swaying body and watched the box. It appeared flawless from the front, but from the side, he could see that its rear panel had loosened, leaving a narrow gap at one corner. Because the flaw was difficult to spot, the staff had probably never repaired it.

The person inside the box must be fully focused, waiting for me to walk past so that he can jump out to scare me.

Scaring people required timing, and the more professional the actor, the better their timing.

Chen Ge thought about it and took out his phone to set a one-minute alarm. He set the alarm tone as Wedding Dress, and he slowly squatted down and slid the phone into the box through the open gap.
